title: Jonas Vingegaard wins Paris-Nice, Isaac del Toro gets Tirreno-Adriatico title
content:
Jonas Vingegaard completed a dominant four-minute victory at Paris-Nice despite just missing out on a final-day stage win to French climber Lenny Martinez.

His triumph, in some ways, makes up for last year’s nightmare experience in which the Dane crashed out and suffered a concussion, while also ensuring that his Visma-Lease a Bike team have now won the race’s last three editions.

Paris-Nice is an eight-stage race from the capital down to the south of France, this year featuring a team time-trial. The route was meant to be spanning more than 1,2oo kilometers but after adverse weather conditions Saturday’s day of racing was shortened leaving the total at just over 1100km.

Vingegaard seized control of the race after breaking away amidst torrential rain on Wednesday’s stage four, while his fellow escapee on that day, Red Bull Bora-Hansgrohe’s Dani Martinez, just held on to his second-place position after crashing heavily on Sunday’s final stage.

At Tirreno-Adriatico, meanwhile, the man that won the previous two Paris-Nice races, Matteo Jorgenson, had to settle for second behind UAE Team Emirates’ Isaac del Toro.

Del Toro became the first Mexican to ever win the race after confirming a decisive lead on Saturday’s queen stage, while Jorgenson became just the first American to podium — after Christian Horner in 2011 and Greg Lemond in 1982 — having overhauled Red Bull’s Giulio Pellizzari for second.

The Italian stage race spans seven days of racing a total of 1,165km from the west to the east coast, including an individual time-trial.

Italy’s sprinter Jonathan Milan won the final stage on home soil for the third consecutive year.

In some ways, it is a shame that Del Toro will not return to northern Italy in May to race Vingegaard at the Giro d’Italia, the latter looking to complete his set of Grand Tour victories.

Having come so close to winning the Giro last season, only being pipped by a superb Simon Yates attack on the Colle delle Finestre on the final mountain stage, UAE Team Emirates have opted to send the 22-year-old to the Tour de France in support of Tadej Pogacar.

Instead, Joao Almeida will lead UAE at the Giro — the Portuguese rider finished second to Vingegaard in last autumn’s Vuelta a Espana.

After a week of stage racing, the cycling world’s attention now turns towards Milan-San Remo on Saturday — where Tadej Pogacar, looking to win this Monument for the first time, will meet two-time winner Mathieu van der Poel.
